reasons: Deviation classification is sound: the grant covers affiliated companies (fallback element 1) but is expressly non-transferable with assignment barred absent Garman's consent (p0033, p0142), so the clause fails the fallback's successor-transfer requirement on a material term — not mere sub-element polish.
The rationale correctly rules out walk-away (perpetual while fees paid, not revocable at Garman's discretion) and does not overstate the defect.

Redline is targeted and reaches the playbook position: contractors/outsourced providers acting on our behalf added to the grant, a successor-assignment carve-out inserted in the general assignment bar, and a conforming cross-reference added to the licensee covenant so the two clauses do not conflict.

Existing protections we do not need to disturb are preserved (Authorized Locations limitation carried through via 'in each case', Garman's consent right retained for all other assignments), so no gratuitous expansion of scope.
Comment is accurate, first-person plural, concise, and states both what changed and the retained limits; it matches the redline text.

The failed minimal-edit heuristic on p0142 (0.620) is explained by the necessary addition of an M&A successor-assignment exception to a short one-sentence clause; the surviving consent requirement is left intact, so the edit is substantively minimal. The mutual ('either party') framing is symmetrical market practice and does not prejudice us.
